main_topics.reason: The user repeatedly asked which RA medications are compatible with pregnancy and how to plan a transition before trying to conceive.
After explaining they had recently started methotrexate, the user asked whether to worry and discussed contraception and the washout period.
The user asked what could happen if pregnancy-compatible medication did not control their RA as well as methotrexate.
The user asked whether RA changes during pregnancy and said they wanted to be prepared for a possible postpartum flare.
The user asked whether pregnancy-compatible medications could also be used while breastfeeding.
The user asked which clinicians to involve and whether to raise pregnancy plans with their rheumatologist now.
The user described being anxious about having to choose between their health and having a baby, then said they felt more reassured.

output.summary: Recently diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis, the user wanted to plan medication choices for trying for a baby in one to two years and learned about pregnancy-compatible options, methotrexate precautions, switching and postpartum planning. The assistant outlined a care-team and preconception plan; the user said the recap matched their understanding and that they left feeling they had a handle on the issue.
